synthesis: scout:record-check-ins matches each Scout kit's GPS (clarity.sc_positions) against its org's open Direct/Staging order addresses and persists one row per (kit, address, hour) into platform.scout_check_ins. It exhausted the production host's memory on 2026-08-12 (~29GB marginal across ~17 concurrent processes, ~30GB headroom) and was disabled (commit 11bc23e2); it stays disabled until the ACs are met. Root cause is a chain, not a single bug: (1) lower(kit_mapping) disables sc_positions' primary-key ordering, making every position read a near-full-table scan; (2) one org's ~255k open addresses get pulled out of ClickHouse into a PHP array by ScoutOpenOrderAddressesQuery, then re-serialized as a `values(...)` SQL literal and pushed BACK into ClickHouse in 2000-row chunks per kit by ScoutCheckInMatchQuery (~5,500 CH round-trips/cycle) -- this round-trip is both the duration and the memory amplifier; (3) `withoutOverlapping(10)` is a lock EXPIRY, not a duration cap, so cycles running 36-209 minutes let a new process start roughly every 10 minutes, driving concurrency to ~17-21 with no ceiling; (4) each process holds its own O(addresses_per_org) copy (the address array, array_chunk's per-kit copy, the accumulating $matches array), so total host memory is O(addresses_per_org x concurrent_processes), unbounded. The intended outcome (this PR, W2+W3): rewrite the match to run server-side in ClickHouse (lifting ScoutCheckInRollupQuery's matches-CTE architecture onto sc_positions instead of scans_hot/cold) so only ~40 match rows/cycle ever cross into PHP, and add a hard, runtime-independent concurrency ceiling, so re-enabling the schedule cannot reproduce the outage. W1 (the sc_positions lower(kit_mapping) projection that makes the ClickHouse side itself fast) is chlocal-owned and out of scope; W4 (flipping the schedule back on + host verification) is an operational, prod-only step gated on production observation, not a code change this PR can complete or prove.

scope.summary: Rewrite scout:record-check-ins' match computation to run entirely server-side in ClickHouse (one statement per unit of work, no PHP-held address list, no values() re-injection), replacing ScoutOpenOrderAddressesQuery + ScoutCheckInMatchQuery's two-query/round-trip design with a single new query class that lifts ScoutCheckInRollupQuery's matches CTE onto clarity.sc_positions. Pair it with a hard concurrency ceiling (W3) that holds independent of cycle duration, so `withoutOverlapping`'s expiry-not-cap defect can no longer drive unbounded concurrent processes. Add the missing peak-memory regression test at a realistic address cardinality (AC6), fix the AC7 silent-failure gap (ClickhouseQuery::query() swallows \Throwable to [] in prod/testing, so the recorder's existing per-org/per-kit try/catch blocks are dead code against ClickHouse failures specifically -- the 94-CH-errors/0-warnings evidence in the incident data proves this happened), and add a parity check between the new matcher and ScoutCheckInRollupQuery on the same proximity/hour-bucket/tie-break domain rule (AC9). Do NOT change the sc_positions schema (W1, chlocal-owned) and do NOT re-enable the schedule (W4, operational/prod-only) in this PR.

proposed_changes.change: NEW query class (name is a suggestion -- ScoutCheckIn + GPS-based, mirroring ScoutCheckInRollupQuery's naming so the two sibling matchers stay discoverable together). One ClickHouse statement: position_window (clarity.sc_positions, lower(kit_mapping) [[= or IN -- design risk 1]], time window) -> bbox prefilter (same BBOX_PAD_DEGREES=0.003 as the rollup/current matcher) -> open_hotlists (clarity.hotlist FINAL, status=Open, length(plate)>3, org/staging filter) -> address_links (zod.public_hotlist_address, DISTINCT + is_staged) -> addresses (zod.public_address, id IN (address_links) prune KEPT alongside the address_links JOIN, extract()+toFloat64OrNull EWKT parsing, no FINAL, _peerdb_is_deleted=0) -> geoDistance <= 160.934 join -> GROUP BY (address_id, hour_bucket) with the same argMin/min tie-break logic (direct-preferred, earliest-fix lat/lng/matched_at) as today's ScoutCheckInMatchQuery output shape. Returns only match rows (~40/cycle per the ticket's cited figure), never an address list.
proposed_changes.reason: This is the substance of AC1: server-side match, nothing large crosses the PHP boundary. It is exactly the extension point ScoutCheckInRollupQuery's docblock names for DEV-1758 ('the CTE is kept on purpose so DEV-1758 can lift the matches stream when it needs an event-style feed') -- reuse, don't rebuild.

proposed_changes.change: Remove openOrderAddressesForOrg()/the org-level address cache and the per-kit $addresses parameter threading; call the new query class once per unit of work (per-org or per-kit -- design risk 1) and insertOrIgnore/firstOrCreate the returned match rows directly, same as today. Keep the existing per-org and per-kit try/catch structure (it is correct; only the swallow underneath it is the bug -- see the ClickhouseQuery.php change below) and the completion-summary/overrun logging.
proposed_changes.reason: Removes the amplifier (root cause 3 in the incident report): no PHP array of ~255k addresses, no array_chunk copy per kit, no values() literal.

proposed_changes.change: Add an opt-in, backward-compatible way for a call site that already has its own try/catch to receive the real exception instead of the swallowed [] -- e.g. a `throwOnFailure: bool = false` parameter on query() that skips the catch's early-return-[] branch in production|testing (default false preserves today's behavior for the ~20 other query classes). The new matcher's call sites in ScoutRecordCheckIns opt in.
proposed_changes.reason: AC7. The org/kit try/catch blocks in ScoutRecordCheckIns already exist and already log distinctly ('org address enumeration failed' / 'kit failed') -- they are simply unreachable for ClickHouse failures today because query()'s catch (lines 29-37) intercepts first. The incident evidence (94 CH-159 errors, 0 matching warnings in a 4h window) proves this is not hypothetical.

proposed_changes.change: W3: a hard concurrency ceiling that holds independent of cycle duration -- e.g. an N-slot Cache::lock semaphore acquired at command start (exit self::SUCCESS with a logged skip if no slot is free) rather than relying on the scheduler's withoutOverlapping expiry. Concrete slot count and mechanism are a design decision (see questions).
proposed_changes.reason: AC4. withoutOverlapping(10) is an expiry, not a cap (root cause 4); nothing in W2 alone bounds concurrency if duration regresses or a downstream dependency (e.g. Postgres) slows down.

questions.q: IN vs equality on lower(kit_mapping) for the new query -- one statement per ORG (kit_mapping IN (...), optimizer may not prune) vs one per KIT (equality, prunes cleanly but ~43 queries/cycle instead of ~12)?

Does the rollup's bbox-prefilter performance profile (tuned against scans, which arrive far less densely than GPS) actually transfer to sc_positions, where fixes land every ~3s and position_window / the bbox may be much larger and less selective?

W3 mechanism: an N-slot Cache::lock semaphore acquired at command start (simple, but a fixed N does not distribute load across orgs) vs per-org queued jobs with HORIZON_SUPERVISOR_*_PROCESSES (the DEV-2347 shape, already reverted once because maxProcesses defaults to 1 and would serialize/collapse throughput ~7x under the OLD architecture's durations)? W2 changes the throughput math the DEV-2347 revert was based on, so the tradeoff needs re-evaluating, not re-assuming the old conclusion.
Does W2 batch the match statement per-org (fewer, larger queries; couples to the IN-vs-equality risk above) or per-kit (more, smaller, individually prunable queries)?

How do AC2 (duration < 5min, measured) and AC3 (memory budget fits headroom, measured) actually get verified, given this pipeline has no production or prod-scale-staging access? A local Docker CH fixture cannot hold 255k real addresses at realistic geo-distribution.

Should the flag/schedule stay disabled even after W2+W3 land here, until W1 (chlocal projection) ships -- given evidence-38238-projection.md explicitly states that on the CURRENT unprojected sc_positions table, both the per-org IN and per-kit equality shapes are slow, so W2+W3 alone may not achieve the AC2 cadence?
questions.answer: Yes -- the brief is explicit that the schedule stays commented out (W4 deferred) and the app.experimental.clarity_scout flag remains the only gate; nothing in this PR re-enables it. The open sub-question is whether W2+W3 alone would even be SUFFICIENT once someone does try to re-enable, which genuinely depends on the unmeasured pre-W1 performance (see the two rows above) -- that residual is left needs-human.

notes: The exact 'the concurrency is load-bearing' / 'currently the only reason the recorder keeps up' conclusion that CLAUDE.md's WRITE-timing rule cites as having 'contributed to an outage' is not just a withdrawn wiki edit -- it is still live in two places in this codebase today: the commented-out schedule block's own explanatory comment (routes/console.php:66) and okf/concepts/scout-check-in-recorder.md's Performance section (line 86) and Gotchas restatement. Both predate the 2026-08-12 OOM and were written during this same ticket's prior (superseded) iteration, commit 102a3430.

Git history on this exact branch shows DEV-2342 was worked through several iterations before this fresh restart (b25a6fe6 -> 55e1bbcc -> f34a5cda -> caab5a46 -> 102a3430 -> 11bc23e2), including trying and reverting a DEV-2347 per-org job dispatcher (maxProcesses=1 serialization concern) and a 90-then-20-minute lock-expiry change. Re-litigating those exact same tradeoffs from scratch is a real risk for the build session; the reverts happened because the OLD (pre-W2) architecture's per-cycle duration made them net-negative -- W2 changes that math and the tradeoffs should be re-derived, not assumed to still hold.

ClickhouseQuery::query()'s swallow-to-[] behavior (app.env in [production, testing]) means the existing 20-ish other query classes across the app share the exact same AC7-class risk; the throwOnFailure opt-in proposed here is scoped to this ticket's call sites only, but is a reusable escape hatch other callers could adopt later.

Laravel's Cache::lock() atomic-lock support works with the app's configured cache stores (database/file are both in play per config/cache.php and .env.example) -- no infra gap for a semaphore-style W3, but there is no existing Cache::lock() usage anywhere in app/ to pattern-match against; it would be a new idiom for this repo (though a standard Laravel one).

The 296,459-row largest hotlist_address group (measured live, see resource_envelope) is addresses-per-HOTLIST, a different axis than the ticket's cited addresses-per-ORG (~255k) figure -- both point at the same ORDER BY id / no-prune problem on zod.public_hotlist_address, but are not directly comparable numbers.

Per laravel-boost-guidelines.md: the new query class should follow the existing static-handle()-method convention (ClickhouseQuery subclasses have no constructors and are not instantiated) -- this is an established, deliberate exception to constructor-promotion guidance, matched by every sibling class in app/Clickhouse/Queries/.

With CH forced unreachable in a production-like env (app.env=production, not the local rethrow branch), the org/kit-level warning log AND report() must actually fire -- proving the swallow no longer eats the signal (today's clickhouse_unreachable_degrades_gracefully_without_crashing test explicitly documents and accepts the swallow; a new test needs to prove the OPPOSITE for the failure-signal path).
